paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God talks, and He talks in two ways. The sky pours forth speech day after day and night after night, and David says it happens "Without speech or language, without a sound to be heard" (Psalm 19:3). Then the psalm turns to the Law of the LORD, which is "perfect, reviving the soul" (Psalm 19:7). The sky shows you that God is great, and His Word tells you what He is like and what He wants.

So why does that matter to YOU? Because David doesn't treat God's Word like a chore. He says it brings joy to the heart, gives light to the eyes, and is "sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb" (Psalm 19:10). I bake cookies all day, and that is a HIGH bar! Time in the Word is not a burden to get through. It's a gift worth leaning toward, with "great reward" in keeping it (Psalm 19:11).

And then David does something I love. He asks, "Who can discern his own errors?" and prays, "Cleanse me from my hidden faults" (Psalm 19:12). He doesn't pretend he's got it all together. He ends by asking that his words and his heart be pleasing to the LORD, "my Rock and my Redeemer" (Psalm 19:14). So look up, friend, open the Word, and then pray like David did. Honestly, that is a great way to start a day.
